newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rises, interbank rate falls late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rises, interbank rate falls late.

text.p: The Thai baht edged higher against the dollar in late trade on Monday following the U.S unit's weakness abroad, dealers said.
The baht strengthened to 25.976/25.981 to the dollar late from 25.988/25.993 early, they added.
The dollar's downside against the baht was still limited due to high liquidity and low baht interest premiums against the U.S. unit.
"There was still some bidding on the dollar today. It is not attractive to hold the baht due to its narrower interest premium against the dollar," said one dealer at a local bank.
Rising liquidity pushed the overnight interbank rate down to 5.75-6.00 percent in late trade from 7.00 in the morning, dealers said.
Dealers said the ample money supply was caused by the gradual entry of some Government Pension Fund (GPF) which was launched last week.
The market expects about 80 billion baht ($3 billion) in money from the Government Pension Fund (GPF) to enter the financial system in stages after the launch.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 7.50/8.00 satangs late compared with 6.50/7.25 in early morning.
